Scripts and tests are written purely against the contract's signatures; expect first-run fixes.

Extra files written beyond the three scripts, three tests and fixtures: tcb/schemas/stpa.schema.json, fmea.schema.json and hazards.schema.json. The gate spec says the builder of gate.mjs writes them (and gate.mjs and its T21 need them), but the brief says to write only the named files. I chose the spec. Delete them if another agent owns them.

The design-check schemas carry `schema_version` (const 1, required) although the spec's field lists omit it: lib.checkFormat requires `schema_version` equal to x-version (CONTRACT 3.4 / 4.7), so the stored objects must carry it. The fmea 'exactly one of finding / na_reason' rule is a `oneOf` of two branches. All schema keywords stay inside the closed validator subset.

Layout: the brief places the scripts at tcb/<name>.mjs next to tcb/lib.mjs, the contract says tcb/scripts/<name>.mjs. Scripts import './lib.mjs'. The tests find the script at tcb/scripts/ first, then tcb/ (findScript), and the wt/ copy test copies lib.mjs from the script's own folder. If the integrator moves scripts to tcb/scripts/ the lib must move with them.

Tests do not use tcb/test/helpers.mjs: each file carries one identical COMMON HELPERS block (makeRoot copying tcb/schemas etc., hash-chained addLedger, run, shape, snapshot, holdLock), as the sibling test files do. Ledger lines are written by hand with the section 3.7 hash rule, so a divergence from lib.verifyLedger will show up as a verifyLedger failure. Synthetic transcripts in compare.test use their own writer with `timestamp` on assistant records (as in probes/transcript-format.md), not helpers.fakeTranscript.

Extra reason slugs not in the specs: protocol-freeze `key-prefix` (named only in spec T9, used for a key whose prefix is another field, also for a cross_field key whose prefix is not its owner_field), `field-name` (freeze: draft `field` differs from the file name) and `field-changed` (amend, the spec's slug for the same condition), `looks`, `predicted-total`, `decision-rules` (plan checks; the schema may report them first as schema-invalid, both are listed); compare `plan-missing`, `plan-invalid`, `no-arm-committed`, `protocol-missing`, `scorer-transcript-missing`, `blind-key-differs` (exit 1, an existing key with other bytes), `boundary-missing:<task>`, `no-key`; gate `fmea-cell-dup`, `hazards-parent-missing`, `model-unreadable`.

protocol-freeze: the default rng seed hashes the canonical draft with `seeds` replaced by the sorted unique list, so the split is independent of seed order (spec T12 needs this). When `sealed/heldout/<field>.json` exists, its stored rng_seed is reused if no --rng-seed is given, so a repeat freeze is a replay. A replay check precedes the 'approval must be newer than the last freeze' rule (spec T2 would otherwise fail). Replay is exit 0 and writes only missing files or a missing seed-split line. A sealed file with other bytes in freeze mode is exit 3 frozen-tampered. Refusals of every exit code after the ce check (also exit 2) append one incident of class refusal followed by a `check` line (fail, or not_run for exit 2); frozen-tampered uses the tamper detail form.

compare: index.json lists `arm_names` as the spec says, so a grep of all of views/blind for arm names would hit index.json; test T5 greps the item files only (the scorer needs the names to fill guess_arm). `arms.<x>.status` is `committed` or `not_run`; with no --scorer-transcript each arm's `rubric_total` is `{status:'not_run'}`. Figures are computed before the run lock is taken (no transcript parse under the lock, CONTRACT 2.1) and only the write and the check line happen under it; an exit 3 appends a tamper incident. The check line `score` is `not_run` when blinding is not run, an arm is not committed, or a transcript or boundary is missing, else `pass`. `within_2x` is 0.5 <= actual/predicted <= 2.

gate: `cut_sha` in gate.json is taken from the last `cut` line even when the cut file is missing or edited (null only with no cut line). A missing or unparseable measures file counts as `measure-missing` only for action lines whose param has gate true and a non-null value. `gate.json` and the check/gate/incident lines are written only when the bytes change or no `gate` line exists. The hazards object and hazards_sha are taken from lib.currentDesign; stpa and fmea are chosen by the same highest-commit-seq rule inside gate.mjs because currentDesign returns only the hazards object.

The selftest case folders hold hash-chained ledgers generated with the same section 3.7 rule as the tests (writer_sha is 64 zeros). Fixture drafts assume `card_schema_version` 1 and guessed types for the analysis plan's `units`, `primary` and `delta` (strings) and `secondary` (string array); the schemas for protocol and analysis-plan were not available to check against. There is no `good` check case for gate (it needs a cut file made by the real script).
lib_change_requests: Export `TcbError` (class with code, exit, detail; constructor `(code, exit, detail)`): all three scripts use `new lib.TcbError(...)` and `instanceof lib.TcbError`.

runMain must learn the stdout `mode` and `dry_run` from the object the script returns: the scripts return `{exit, mode, dry_run, result, reasons}` and also set `ctx.mode` and `ctx.dry_run`. If runMain reads neither, every line prints mode null and dry_run false and the dry-run tests fail.

withRunLock must accept `retries` in its options object (scripts pass `{script, ce, proc, now, retries}` with `retries` = threshold lock_retries when present), and `lib.realProc({exe})` must accept `{}` when proc_exe is absent from the thresholds (the scripts treat proc_exe and lock_retries as optional, but tcb/thresholds.json currently ships neither).

`thresholds(root).all` must expose the params map (name to {value, unit, source, gate, line?}) or `{params}`; gate.mjs reads action lines from it (params carrying `line: {measure, op}`), `.get` for the threshold value and `.isGate` for gate-ness. The shipped tcb/thresholds.json has no `line` on unverifiable_share_max and marks coverage_floor `gate: false`; CONTRACT 3.20 wants `line` on both (the tests overwrite the root copy themselves).

`loadSchema(root, 'card')` must return the parsed schema with its `x-version` (protocol-freeze compares `card_schema_version` with it). The protocol and analysis-plan schemas must accept the shapes in the tests (CONTRACT 3.18): the tests' analysis plan uses string `units`, `primary`, `delta` and array `secondary`; if the schema types differ, adjust mkPlan in protocol-freeze.test.mjs.

`recordIncident(root, handle, {ctx, ce, cls, detail, now})` must write a line whose data is `{class, detail}` (the tests read `data.class` and `data.detail.tamper`). The shipped `tcb/thresholds.json` also lacks lock_retries, proc_exe, user_files and several names listed in CONTRACT 3.20.

Library functions the scripts await may be sync or async; all calls are awaited except `lib.sessionTranscripts`, `lib.transcriptsForFolder`, `lib.parseTranscript`, `lib.verifyLedger`, `lib.lastLine` and `lib.thresholds(...).get/isGate`, which are used synchronously (as the contract describes them).
